subject: psychology

moments.title: The Nature of Love
moments.body: Harlow's APA presidential address shows infant rhesus monkeys clinging to cloth surrogates rather than wire feeders.

quote.text: Man cannot live by milk alone.

moments.takeaway: Attachment is not reducible to feeding.

moments.title: Total isolation studies
moments.body: Isolated monkeys show severe social and emotional pathology, recovering only partially with peer 'monkey therapists'.
moments.takeaway: Early social experience has enduring developmental effects.

moments.title: Ethical reckoning
moments.body: Critics including Peter Singer cite Harlow's 'pit of despair' studies in the emerging animal-rights movement.
moments.takeaway: Foundational findings sit alongside foundational ethical concerns.

now.title: Contact comfort revisited
now.body: Skin-to-skin and kangaroo care for premature infants are mainstream paediatric practice.
now.open_questions: How do digital substitutes for caregiver interaction affect infant attachment?

reflection: Harlow's work is taught both as landmark research and as a case study in research ethics.
